successors.note: 27 June 1869: Goryōkaku handed to Kuroda Kiyotaka; the island 'was renamed Hokkaido' on 20 September 1869 (Republic of Ezo page).

capitals.name: Hakodate (Goryōkaku)
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Hakodate; the defences centred on the Goryōkaku star fortress. Coordinates are the researcher's placement of Goryōkaku.

rulers.name: Enomoto Takeaki
rulers.title: sōsai (president)
rulers.note: Elected president on 27 January 1869 by a vote limited to samurai; Matsudaira Tarō vice-president. He led the fleet from 4 October 1868 and surrendered on 26 June 1869.

correction.text: the island of Ezo, now Hokkaido, which the Republic claimed

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a break-away state Cliopatria lacks (its Tokugawa Shogunate row ends in 1869 with Hokkaido inside it). The page's territory: the Republic 'claimed the island of Ezo, now Hokkaido' and held Hakodate, Matsumae and Esashi; 'End of 1868: The rebels held the whole region'. The whole island (about 81,000 km2 by the gazetteer) is the claim; the interior was not garrisoned on any page. No page gives an area.

ledger.note: December 1868: Enomoto's fleet takes Hakodate. The fleet left Shinagawa on 4 October 1868, 'arrived at Hakodate' on 3 December and the town was captured 'about December 8' by some 4,000 troops; the Republic was proclaimed on 27 January 1869 (infobox 'Established January 27, 1869') with Enomoto as sōsai. The page does not name Hakodate's defenders; the new government is the researcher's reading.
18 December 1868: Matsumae Castle is captured. 'December 18, 1868: Matsumae Castle was captured'; the Matsumae had fought as the Tate clan (Matsumae Domain page).
28 December 1868: Esashi is captured. 'End of 1868: The rebels held the whole region.'

region.text: the rest of Ezo, which the Republic claimed

ledger.note: End of 1868: the island is the Republic's claim. The page says 'The Republic claimed the island of Ezo, now Hokkaido'; no page garrisons the interior, so the researcher draws the claim (confidence 1).

April 1869: the imperial fleet and 7,000 infantry reach Hokkaido. Imperial forces 'won the Battle of Hakodate and surrounded Goryōkaku'; the page gives no exact days for the landing. The empire-of-japan dossier opens its contest with the Republic in January 1868 over northern Honshu and Ezo.

26-27 June 1869: Enomoto surrenders. 'Enomoto surrendered on June 26'; 'Goryōkaku was handed to Kuroda Kiyotaka on June 27, 1869'. The History of Hokkaido page says the rebellion was defeated in May 1869; the Republic of Ezo page's dates are used.

region.text: the island of Ezo, now Hokkaido, which the Republic claimed

ledger.note: 27 June 1869: the Republic is disestablished. Ezochi 'was then annexed and placed under the Hakodate Prefectural Government' (History of Hokkaido); on 20 September 1869 the island was renamed Hokkaido. The Matsumae regained their domain name on 24 June 1869.

wars.name: Battle of Hakodate
wars.outcome: The Republic took Hakodate, Matsumae and Esashi in December 1868; imperial forces landed in April 1869 with 7,000 men, won the Battle of Hakodate and surrounded Goryōkaku; Enomoto surrendered on 26 June 1869.
wars.note: The last campaign of the Boshin War, called the Hakodate War on the Matsumae Domain page.

certainty.note: Only the towns the pages name (Hakodate, Matsumae, Esashi) were held; the rest of the island is a claim.

sources.title: Republic of Ezo
sources.note: Infobox established 27 Jan 1869, disestablished 27 June 1869, capital Hakodate; 3 Dec 1868 fleet at Hakodate; ~8 Dec Hakodate captured; 18 Dec Matsumae Castle; 28 Dec Esashi; April 1869 imperial landing of 7,000; 26-27 June 1869 surrender; claimed the island of Ezo.

sources.title: History of Hokkaido
sources.note: Enomoto Takeaki led Tokugawa loyalists who temporarily occupied the island; 'commonly but mistakenly called the Republic of Ezo'; defeated in May 1869 (the Republic of Ezo page gives 26-27 June); Ezochi annexed to the Hakodate Prefectural Government; Hokkaido renamed 1869.

sources.title: Matsumae Domain
sources.note: The Matsumae allied with the Ōu-Etsu alliance, fought the Hakodate War as the Tate clan; castle moved to Tate Castle in 1868; domain name reinstated 24 June 1869.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from three pages (Republic of Ezo, History of Hokkaido, Matsumae Domain). Type rebel (a Tokugawa-loyalist break-away state). Start is the fleet's capture of Hakodate in December 1868, not the proclamation of 27 January 1869 (infobox), so that the state is drawn from the winter of 1868; a reviewer may prefer 1869. End 27 June 1869. Mismatches with sister dossiers: empire-of-japan opens a contest with 'republic-of-ezo' in January 1868 over northern Honshu and Ezo and closes it, with the gain, in May 1869 (its page 'The siege of Hakodate came to an end in May 1869'); the Republic of Ezo page gives surrender on 26 June and the handover of Goryōkaku on 27 June 1869, and tokugawa-shogunate has June. Hakodate's defenders before 8 December 1868 are not named on the page. The matsumae-domain dossier carries the mirror losses of 18 and 28 December 1868 and the regain in June 1869. Not on the pages: Ōuetsu Reppan Dōmei details, the Kaiyō Maru, foreign recognition (the page says Nagai Naoyuki tried to reach legations in Hakodate; success is not reported). Gazetteer: no 'Matsumae' or 'Esashi' place (coordinate circles). Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
